acceptedWorkstreams.title: Badge proof that survives sharing: a public verification page plus a share caption that states exactly what the badge proves
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The accepted workstream makes the badge prove a completed cohort workflow; this idea makes that proof visible to the people who see the shared badge. Approach: 1) give each issued badge a public verification page (zedu.chat/certified/{badge-id}) that shows the holder, the course, the date issued and the workflow completed, with no personal data beyond what the holder chose to share; 2) ship a ready-to-paste LinkedIn caption that states what the badge proves ('completed the 5-lesson cohort-running course and set up a real cohort workspace') so sharers never overclaim; 3) add one FAQ line for viewers asking how to check a badge is real. Done when: a test badge can be verified from a public link, the caption template states only what the course actually certifies, and the course completion message links to the verification page. Measured: every issued badge has a working verification link; the caption text is reviewed against the course syllabus. Why this fits: a shareable badge is worthless if viewers cannot check it, and most fake-badge problems come from captions claiming more than the course covers; this closes both gaps without adding lessons or changing the assessment design.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Make the educator badge prove a completed cohort workflow with five assessed lessons
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Use one fictional cohort throughout five 10-15 minute lessons: plan its channel structure; write the welcome and announcements; organise resources and learner questions; prepare a Buzz teaching session; and run a weekly review with human follow-up. Each lesson ends with one observable practice output and two scenario questions, rather than passive video completion. Verify all app labels and capabilities against the current product before scripting; reuse the existing help articles and tutorial work rather than re-create them. Deliver one coherent course-authoring pack: five timed scripts, an objective-to-practice-to-question matrix, ten questions with answers and explanations, a final synthetic cohort exercise and rubric, completion/badge wording, and landing copy. Completion threshold is a proposed team decision, not an invented existing certification. Acceptance: all five lessons fit the time budget; every stated capability has dated evidence; each objective is assessed; a reviewer can score the worked exercise consistently; badge copy states what was completed and promises no professional accreditation or employment outcome. Measure pilot completion, question errors and rubric disagreements only with permissioned real data; use labelled synthetic examples until then. This fills the assessment-design gap absent from the existing generic audit/execution proposal. No badge issuance, public course launch, learner recruitment, account changes or publication.
